answer: Every new identity posts a 500 POA mirror bond and a fingerprint hash into a public mirror registry. When a second fingerprint mirrors an existing one closely, both bonds freeze and three random jurors run an opal audit in 24 hours: a confirmed duplicate slashes both bonds and burns the identity. The bond grows with each fake: the first costs 500 POA, the tenth 5,000, the hundredth 50,000, so 100 fakes together cost 2,525,000 POA. Between audits, sparrow spot-checks pick one identity in ten per epoch; a chosen key must show fresh hardware proof in ten minutes or its bond freezes five epochs.
